clauses.text:
Executive Order 10904
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN CERTAIN CARRIERS REP­
RESENTED BY THE NEW YORK  
HARBOR CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE  
COMMITTEE AND CERTAIN OF  
THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
certain carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, designated in the List of Carriers 
attached hereto and hereby made a part 
hereof, and certain of their employees 
represented by the Lighter Captains’  
Union, Local 996, I.L.A., a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160) , I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by carriers represented by the 
New York Harbor Carriers’ Conference 
Committee, or by their employees, in the 
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

reviews.reasons: Identity: EO 10904, signed 1961-01-12 (Dwight D. Eisenhower), 26 FR 279; number, date, signatory and title agree between the held FR OCR text and the OFR catalog. Inventory: the order has two operative commands, the board clause (create a three-member board, member disinterest, report within thirty days) and the section 10 no-change sentence; the rest is recitals, signature and the carrier lists, so the two-clause inventory is complete. Board clause: the held NMB report's cover and letter of transmittal are dated 1961-03-06 and submit the report herewith; under owner rule D-20261108-board-rule (haloander-decisions item 2) the board's command ends by completion of task on that date; actor and mechanism are stated correctly and the receipt caveat is accurate. No-change clause: 1961-03-06 + 30 days = 1961-04-05 (inclusive), exclusive 1961-04-04; arithmetic checked; whole_order_end equals the later clause end. Earlier end: no held order text names the order other than its own printing and the report (cruden), the only OFR note is the EO 12553 revocation (1986-02-25), which the claim records as a later event and formal disposition, and the order has no own-terms end earlier than the report. The report came after the order's thirty-day deadline (1961-02-11); the held report itself records that the parties stipulated extensions of the reporting time to not later than 1961-03-11 and the President approved the request after the NMB's advice of 1961-02-21, so the board did not lapse before reporting. The rationale's 'no extension ... is flagged' refers to the exception screen for extending orders, and none exists (cruden); recording the presidential approval of the extension as a later event would be fuller, but it does not change any date, actor or mechanism and the owner rule fixes the end at the report date. Savings: EO 12553 has no saving language; the report and any agreement rest on the Railway Labor Act and the parties' acts; correctly stated. Searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) are bounded and honestly described; status NO is consistent. All quoted spans and file hashes verified against the bytes.

EO 10904 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.
